Now come and break this door."

You rise slowly, the way a beaten man does, and shuffle to the door in your hobbles. Through the gap you call out in Goblin, flat as a hanged man: "Greyshaft's books are honest, Sergeant, honest as the knife at my sister's throat, and I speak from a cold heart and a full belly. Now come and break this door."

It lands. The cloak at Tessa's neck eases his blade a finger's breadth, satisfied. The Foreman, standing by the desk, lets his breath go. For one moment he thinks he has won.

Your chained fists come down on the lantern. Glass cracks, and the oil jumps in a bright sheet across the desk, over the contract, over his sleeve. The Foreman cries out and tears at the cloth, throws himself back and beats the flame out against the wall, and he is unhurt, but the floor between him and his cloaks is a burning pool. Smoke rolls along the ceiling.

Outside, Dreg's voice has stopped bellowing. In its place there is a silence, and then the crash of a spear-butt on oak, and another. Whoever is on the other side of that door has heard you say the one thing a man like you never says, and has understood it exactly.

The Foreman has not waited to watch. He's already at the narrow door to the bedchamber, dragging the bar off its pegs with both hands, and the cloaks with bows are turning to face you, torn between the fire and their orders. Tessa is working at her wall ring with a hairpin. She hasn't got it yet. The blade is still at her neck.

It is your turn again, with a burning room, a door shaking on its hinges, and the bows swinging toward you. Your wrists are in iron, your ankles are hobbled, and you are at 1 hit point. What does Korvash do?

sheet.name: Korvash Emberhide
sheet.opening: Korvash Emberhide, a hulking red-scaled dragonborn barbarian (Chaotic Good, loud, proud, quick to anger; ideal Charity; bond: he keeps his word no matter what; flaw: inflexible), arrives at dusk in a lowland market town near the foot of the mountains, driving off a pack of bullies shaking down a family of herders, as he has done for years. His past, which the opening must respect: he comes from a clan of mountain herders. When he was young, hobgoblins of the Iron Tallies warband, led by a tin-masked captain named Gorrak Vael (who notches a rod for every raid), overran his village. His father Dargan held the narrow Goat's Throat pass, losing a hand and then his life, so the herd and the children could flee; Korvash swore to him, with his blood on his hands, to protect the weak. His younger sister Tessa was lost in the raid and her fate is UNKNOWN: he never saw her fall and has never stopped wondering, so she must not be confirmed alive or dead unless discovered in play. The survivors fled to Harrowmere, where his aunt Veshra raised him and still sends word by travelers. The clan built a cairn at the Goat's Throat, which he has never had the heart to revisit. His shame at being too young to stand beside his father is why he is loud and makes sure everyone knows he is standing. He carries his father's second-best greataxe with Dargan's ember-red scale-sash tied to the haft. Hook for the opening: just after the bullies flee, a frightened young herder or a traveler brings him word, perhaps carried from Aunt Veshra, that a hobgoblin warband bearing a tin-masked captain and a notched rod has been seen again, or that something connected to the Goat's Throat has turned up. This pulls him toward an oath-bound choice: someone weak is in immediate danger, he promises to help, and keeping that word will lead him back toward the mountains and the questions about Tessa. You get to your feet slowly, the way a beaten man does, and shuffle toward the door in your hobbles. You lean to the gap and say it flat and loud in Goblin, like a hanged man reading out his sentence. Greyshaft's books are honest, Sergeant, honest as the knife at my sister's throat, and I speak from a cold heart and a full belly. Now come and break this door.

Dreg gets it. A moment of silence on the other side of the oak, then a roar, and the thud of a spear-butt on the planks. It comes again, and then something much heavier, a bench or a beam, driven against the door by a dozen shoulders.

Then you swing your chained fists for the lantern, and the hobbles betray you. Your feet tangle in their own chain. You go down hard against the edge of the desk, and your swing goes wide. The lantern rocks on its base, throws its light across the ceiling, and stays upright. Cloak A makes a grab at you. The big cloak, B, lunges for your collar, and you roll out of his hands, your whole weight and a lifetime of wrestling goats behind it. They back off with their hands open, and for a heartbeat nobody touches you.

Across the room, Tessa's face goes blank, then fierce. Her chained wrist twists once behind her back, and the lock gives. You hear it click. Her hand is free, hidden at her side. The cloak with the blade at her neck hasn't noticed.

The Foreman is standing by the barred bedchamber door with his hands inside his sleeves, and his face has gone the colour of tallow. "Hold the door," he says, small and fast. "Hold the girl. Keep the big one off the lantern." The crossbows have swung from you to the door. Behind it, the ram strikes again, and the bar creaks in its brackets.

It is your turn, with the lantern still burning on the desk beside you and the Foreman three paces away. You are on the floor at 1 hit point, in iron, with a sister about to move and six cloaks in the room. What does Korvash do?

entries.text: notebook: updated The Greyshaft Foreman

You slam your chained fists down on the lantern. It bursts off the desk in a spray of glass and burning oil, and the Foreman throws himself aside with a hiss. The flame skims his sleeve and dies on the stone. Fire runs across the floor between him and his cloaks, and for a heartbeat the room is smoke and shouting.

A grey cloak hits you from the side with the flat of a blade. You hear the crack of it before you feel it.

You wake in a different light. The shutters have been ripped away, and thin winter sun lies across a floor that is scorched black and trampled with boots. The air smells of old smoke. It is about one in the afternoon, and you have 1 hit point. The iron is off your wrists. Someone cut it away with a cold chisel. Your wrists are raw, and a clean cloth is wound around each.

Gorrak Vael is crouched beside you. His mask is still gone, and the long seam of burn stands plain in the light. A fresh linen binding shows under his torn shirt, and the rod is back at his belt, one notch fresh. "Easy," he says, low, in Common. "You are not dying. Be quiet and listen."

He lays Dargan's greataxe on the floor beside you, with the ember-red sash knotted at the haft. "It was in the rack by the door. Dreg found it."

Behind him the outer room is full of Tallies. Dreg stands by the broken door with a bleeding scalp, Brun is at his shoulder with a bandaged arm, and Krell leans on the wall with a splint on his swollen hand. A dozen more spears hold the stair beyond. At the far end of the room is the narrow door to the Foreman's bedchamber, and it is barred from the inside.

"The Foreman, four cloaks, the chest with the book, and your sister," Gorrak says. "They took her in with them when the oil went up. He has a knife on her and he will not open. We have held this room for three hours. He sends out one message." His good eye is on yours. "He wants you. Only you. At the door, with the axe laid down. He says he will talk to the man who keeps his word."

From behind the door, very faintly, you hear the click of brass beads.

You are at 1 hit point, with the axe at your hand and the Tallies at your back. Your sister is behind a barred door with a knife at her throat. What does Korvash do?

entries.text: notebook: updated Gorrak Vael

"Come and break this door," you call through the gap, in the flat voice of a hanged man, and the Foreman almost smiles. He does not hear the joke. His lips are still moving over the count when your chained fists come down across the lantern on his desk.

It bursts. Burning oil runs across the desk and the Foreman's sleeve and down onto the floor between him and his cloaks. He screams, once, small and high, and tries to beat out his own arm. Tessa's wall-ring lock clicks open in her fingers, unseen. Five of the six grey cloaks stare at the man who paid them, burning, and drop their bows. The sixth does not.

An arrow takes you in the chest. A second finds you on the floor. You hear Tessa's voice, thin and furious, saying your name, and her small hands are on you, pressing, pressing. Then she is gone, and the dark comes.

You wake in a bed, which is the first strange thing. The second is that nothing hurts as much as it ought to. It is about two in the afternoon on the day after midwinter's eve. You have 1 hit point. The ledger-house is much emptier than you remember. The shutters are open, the walk is full of grey daylight, and the burn on the floor has been scrubbed to a black stain. The big table is back against the wall, and the Foreman is not in it. The desk is just a desk.

Tessa sits on the edge of your cot with a bowl of broth, and she is the first thing you see when your eyes focus. Her wrist is bandaged where the iron was, her split lip is crusted, and she looks as though she hasn't slept. "Don't," she says, before you can speak. "Drink first. You've been out four hours. You nearly didn't come back."

She tells it in short pieces while you swallow. The Foreman died of the burn, quickly, before the cloaks could decide what to do. Five of them gave up their weapons. The sixth kept shooting until Dreg's spear came through the door. Dreg and Brun and twenty Tallies took the walk, and nobody had the stomach to fight them. Gorrak lives; Krell lives. The hanging beam stands empty.

Dargan's greataxe leans against the wall by your bed, with the ember-red sash still tied to the haft. Tessa found it in the bedchamber beside the Foreman's papers and carried it in herself. The horn charm lies on the blanket beside your hand.

"There's one more thing," she says. She nods at the doorway. "The chest. It's sitting in the next room with a Tally on either side. Nobody's opened it. Gorrak says it's yours."

Gorrak Vael stands in the door. He has no mask, and the burn from jaw to ear is plain in the daylight. He holds his notched rod in one hand and a key chain in the other, and behind him on the walk Dreg is waiting with his spears grounded. He looks at you, and then at the chest in the next room.

"The Foreman's chain came off his body," he says. "I have not used it. Whatever is in that book is my name and forty other men's, and I would rather you stood at my shoulder when it is read." He holds out the keys. "Or you may burn it unread. I leave it to the man who burned the first one."

You have 1 hit point, your axe, your sister, and a captain with a key. What does Korvash do?

You drop behind a boulder, out of the archers' line, and shout your terms down the slope in Goblin: call off the bowmen, and meet you at the ford-stones with blade and shield, no ambush. If you put him down, he and his nine lay down their arms and walk to Harrowmere to answer. If he beats you, your spears go home and the barrel is his.

Then you whistle two notes back toward the gully, and a minute later Ushk and Hale come up the goat-path behind you, quiet as wind. Ushk takes in the whole yard in a glance. Hale says only, "He'll take it. He's the kind who can't leave a challenge lying," and spits. You check your breath in your chest, the slow fire there, and the rage waiting like a coal beneath it.

Brakk takes his time. The yard is silent. At last, in the same flat voice: "Done. My bowmen come down off the roof. You come down alone. Your Tallies stay on the ridge." Two archers lower their bows and climb down. You can see the others fall back to the fold-house wall, shields grounded, watching. It is the kind of promise a man like him keeps, because it costs him nothing to keep and a great deal to break in front of his own men.

You walk down the goat-path alone, with the axe in your hands and the sun at your back. It's about half past seven. The ford-stones are a ring of flat grey boulders in the shallows, with a dry shelf of gravel in front of them, thirty feet across. Brakk comes out of the yard to meet you at the near edge. He is big for a hobgoblin and grey at the temples, a heavy round shield on one arm, longsword in the other, and the ring in his ear catches the light. He stops at ten paces and looks you over, the red scales, the axe, the sash tied at the haft.

"Dargan's," he says. "He'd have been proud. Pity he's not here." He lifts the sword. "Say when."

Behind him his nine stand in a half-ring with shields down. Behind you, on the ridge, Ushk and Hale and the spears watch in silence. There's frost on the gravel and the stream is running loud. Your rage is ready, and so is your breath. You have 23 hit points and a plan.

sheet.opening: Korvash Emberhide, a hulking red-scaled dragonborn barbarian (Chaotic Good, loud, proud, quick to anger; ideal Charity; bond: he keeps his word no matter what; flaw: inflexible), arrives at dusk in a lowland market town near the foot of the mountains, driving off a pack of bullies shaking down a family of herders, as he has done for years. His past, which the opening must respect: he comes from a clan of mountain herders. When he was young, hobgoblins of the Iron Tallies warband, led by a tin-masked captain named Gorrak Vael (who notches a rod for every raid), overran his village. His father Dargan held the narrow Goat's Throat pass, losing a hand and then his life, so the herd and the children could flee; Korvash swore to him, with his blood on his hands, to protect the weak. His younger sister Tessa was lost in the raid and her fate is UNKNOWN: he never saw her fall and has never stopped wondering, so she must not be confirmed alive or dead unless discovered in play. The survivors fled to Harrowmere, where his aunt Veshra raised him and still sends word by travelers. The clan built a cairn at the Goat's Throat, which he has never had the heart to revisit. His shame at being too young to stand beside his father is why he is loud and makes sure everyone knows he is standing. He carries his father's second-best greataxe with Dargan's ember-red scale-sash tied to the haft. Hook for the opening: just after the bullies flee, a frightened young herder or a traveler brings him word, perhaps carried from Aunt Veshra, that a hobgoblin warband bearing a tin-masked captain and a notched rod has been seen again, or that something connected to the Goat's Throat has turned up. This pulls him toward an oath-bound choice: someone weak is in immediate danger, he promises to help, and keeping that word will lead him back toward the mountains and the questions about Tessa. Invent only original places and people; keep it grounded in the SRD's monsters (hobgoblins, goblins, bugbears, wolves, etc.).
